description: A subtle, straight embankment or raised‐causeway feature visible as a narrow, linear positive relief ridge in the DTM hillshade. It trends NE–SW (~045°) over ~1 200 m, with very low slope (~1–2°) and uniform width (~6–8 m). In the NIR layer, vegetation atop this ridge shows slightly lower reflectance (darker tones) relative to surrounding forest, suggesting deeper, more moisture‐retentive anthropogenic soils (terra preta) or compacted organic fill.

A second linear feature, trending NW–SE (~135°), visible in the DTM curvature derivative as a straight line of concave–convex transitions. It spans ~900 m, width ~5–7 m, with accompanying paired shallow ditches on either side (total corridor ~15 m). The VNIR true‐color composite shows a faint alignment of slightly yellower canopy along this axis, consistent with periodic moisture stress patterns over buried channels.
